Abu al-Bakhtari said: "As for me, I think you should seize him, imprison him in a room, bind his shackles, seal the door of the room, leave him, and send him his food and drink, and wait for the calamity of fate to befall him until he dies there, as others died before him, such as the poets Zuhayr and al-Nabighah; he is only like one of them."

Then the old man from Najd cried out and said: "Evil is the opinion you have held. You intend to take the man and imprison him, and you will complete his reward, and those around you have heard of him, [so they will soon rise up and snatch him from your hands] [[Addition from Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/98.]] and fight you on his behalf until they take him from you."

They said: "The old man is right." Then Hisham ibn Amr, who was of the Banu Amir ibn Lu'ayy, said: "As for me, I think you should load him on a camel and send him out from among you, so that he will not harm you, for whatever befell him will not harm you once he has gone from you, and he will be gone, and his affair will be in others' hands." Iblis said: "Evil is your opinion. You intend to take a man who has corrupted your foolish ones, and send him out to others, who will corrupt them as he corrupted you. Have you not seen the sweetness of his speech, the eloquence of his tongue, and how he captures hearts by what is heard of his talk? By Allah, if you do so, then he will go around to the Arabs and they will gather against you, and then he will come to you and expel you from your lands and kill your nobles."

They said: "By Allah, the old man is right."

Abu Jahl said: "I will certainly advise you with an opinion other than which I see no other: I think we should take one youth from every clan of Quraysh, a strong lad and of noble lineage, then give each one of them a sharp sword, and they should strike him with the single blow of one man. When they have killed him, his blood will be scattered among all the tribes, and I do not think the Banu Hashim will be able to fight all of Quraysh, and if they see that, they will accept the blood-money, so Quraysh will pay its diya, and we will be relieved." Iblis said: "This youth has spoken truly, and this is the best of your opinions; the saying is what he has said, I see no other."

So they dispersed upon Abu Jahl's proposal, though they were still gathered. Then Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him of that, and commanded him not to sleep on the bed where he usually slept. At that point Allah permitted him to leave for Medina. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honour his face, to sleep in his bed, and said: "Wrap yourself in my cloak, for no matter that you dislike will reach you."

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) went out, taking a handful of dust. Allah took their sight away from him, and he began scattering the dust over their heads while reciting: "We have placed shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up" [Ya-Sin: 8], and he went to the cave of Thawr, entered it with Abu Bakr, and left Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, in Makkah to deliver the deposits (wada'i') that had been left with him, for the deposits used to be placed with him because of his truthfulness and trustworthiness. The polytheists were keeping watch over Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was on the bed of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), thinking that he was the Prophet. When morning came they rushed at him and saw that it was Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.

Allah had turned back their plot, and there was not a single man of them but had dust placed upon his head.

They said: "Where is your companion?"

He said: "I do not know." So they followed his tracks and sent men in pursuit of him. When they reached the mountain and passed the cave, they saw on its entrance a spider's web and said: "If he had entered here, there would not be a spider's web at its door." He remained there three days, then he came to Medina. That is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: "And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to confine you" [[See Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/315, and Tarikh al-Tabari: 2/97–99.]].

Ata' and Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: "to imprison you." Aban ibn Tha'lab and Abu Hatim said: "to wound you with injuries and blows." And he recited:

I said: "Woe to you! What is in your document?" They said: "The caliph has become afflicted with an ailment."

[[Ibn Kathir attributed it in al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah: 8/153 to Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah.]]

It was also said: its meaning is "to mock you."

He said: "Yes, [they intend] to mock me and kill me or expel me." He said: "Who told you this?"

He said: "My Lord."

He said: "What a fine Lord your Lord is. So enjoin upon your Lord what is good."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I enjoin Him? Rather, He enjoins me to do good." [231] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/299, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/314.]]

Al-Hasan said: "They say, and Allah says." Al-Dahhak said: "They devise, and Allah devises." "Allah is the best of planners": He is the best of those who rescued you from them and destroyed them.

"And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, meaning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith: 'We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this.'" Al-asatir is the plural of a plural, and its root is from the verb "saṭara," meaning "he wrote." Its singular is "saṭr," then the plural "asṭār" or "suṭūr," then these two combine into "asāṭir" and "asāṭīr." It was also said: the singular of al-asatir is "usṭūrah" and "usṭār."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 8, verse 27–31:

O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger

Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated to me that Abu Sufyan set out from Makkah, and Jibril (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Abu Sufyan is at such-and-such a place."

So the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Abu Sufyan is at such-and-such a place, so go out to him, and keep it secret." [229] He said: A man among the hypocrites wrote to them, "Muhammad intends to attack you, so take your precautions." So Allah the Exalted revealed the verse. [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 9/291.]]

And al-Suddi said: They would hear something from the Prophet (ﷺ) and then spread it, until it reached the polytheists.

This was because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged the Jews of Qurayzah for twenty-one nights. They asked the Messenger of Allah for a settlement on the same terms that their brothers, the Banu al-Nadir, had accepted, on condition that they might go to their brothers at Adhri'at and Jericho in the land of Syria. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to grant them that, except that they should submit to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh. They refused and said: "Send Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir to us," for he was a counsellor to them, because his dependents, his property and his children were with them. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent him, and he came to them. They said: "O Abu Lubabah, what do you think? Should we submit to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh?" Abu Lubabah pointed with his hand to his throat, indicating that it meant slaughter. He said: "Do not do it."

Abu Lubabah said: "By Allah, my feet did not move from their place until I knew that I had betrayed Allah and the Messenger." When this verse was revealed, he bound himself to one of the pillars of the mosque and said: "By Allah, I will not taste food or drink until I die or Allah forgives me." He remained for seven days, tasting no food or drink, until he fell unconscious. Then Allah forgave him. It was said to him: "O Abu Lubabah, Allah has forgiven you."

He said: "No, by Allah, I will not release myself until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the one who releases me." So he came to him, and he untied him with his own hand. Then Abu Lubabah said: "Part of the completion of my repentance is that I abandon the house of my people in which I committed the sin, and that I strip myself of my property." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A third will suffice you if you give it in charity." [230] [[See Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 9/292. It is well known that Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet, peace be upon them both, came to release him, but he refused, and the Messenger of Allah said: "Fatimah is a part of me," and so he was released. Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah said: This verse was revealed concerning the killing of Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him. [[The same source.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The meaning of the verse is: do not show him the truth that pleases him from you, and then oppose him in secret by turning to something else.

Ibn Abbas said: "Do not betray Allah" by abandoning His obligations, "and the Messenger" by abandoning his sunnah, "and do not betray your trusts."

Al-Suddi said: If they betray Allah and the Messenger, they have betrayed their trusts.

According to this interpretation, His saying "and betray" (wa-takhunu) is in the accusative as an answer to the prohibition.

The Arabs put the answer to a prohibition in the accusative, just as it is put in the accusative after the fa'.

It was also said: it is in the accusative by way of sarf (change of construction), as in the words of the poet:

Do not forbid a trait while you yourself practise its like; it is a great disgrace upon you when you do it.

Al-Akhfash said: it is a conjunction with what precedes it of the prohibition, its meaning being: "and do not betray your trusts."

Mujahid recited "amanatikum" in the singular. They differed concerning this [verse]. Ibn Abbas said: it is what is hidden from people's eyes of the obligations of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the deeds over which Allah has entrusted His servants; He says: do not violate them.

Ibn Zayd said: the meaning of "trusts" here is the religion, and these hypocrites were entrusted by Allah with His religion, but they betrayed it, since they displayed faith and concealed disbelief.

Qatadah said: The religion of Allah is a trust, so render to Allah what He has entrusted you with of His obligations and limits. Whoever has a trust upon him, let him return it to the one who entrusted him with it.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: a way out from doubtful matters in religion. Ikrimah said: deliverance. Al-Dahhak said: clarity. Muqatil said: a rescuer.

Ibn Zayd said: a discrimination that Allah places in their hearts between truth and falsehood, so that they recognise it and bear witness to it.

Al-furqan is a verbal noun like al-rahman and al-nuqsan.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 8, verses 32–35**

﴿وَإِذْ قالُوا اللَّهُمَّ﴾ The verse was also revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn ʿAlqama ibn Kinda, of the Banu ʿAbd al-Dar.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recounted the stories of the earlier generations, al-Nadr said: "If I wished, I could say something like this. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients" ﴿إِنْ هذا إِلَّا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾, which they had in their books.

ʿUthman ibn Maz'un said to him: "Fear Allah, for Muhammad speaks the truth." He said: "I too speak the truth." ʿUthman said: "Muhammad says: there is no god but Allah." He said: "I too say: there is no god but Allah. But this (refers to) the affair of Allah," meaning the idols. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf: 81). Al-Nadr said: "Do you not see that Muhammad has agreed with me in what I say?" meaning his statement ﴿If the Most Merciful had a son﴾.

al-Mughira ibn al-Walid said to him: "By Allah, he did not agree with you, but he says: 'It was not for the Most Merciful to have a son.'"

Al-Nadr grasped this and said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You﴾.

﴿إِنْ كانَ هذا هُوَ الْحَقَّ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ﴾ — ﴿هُوَ﴾ is an ʿimad (the word that stands between two statements, without which the meaning is incomplete; the Basrans call it ḍamīr al-faṣl, the separating pronoun), and it serves as emphasis and a connective in the speech. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ is in the accusative as the predicate of ﴿كان﴾. ﴿فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ كما أمطرتها على قوم لوط﴾ ("then rain down upon us stones from the sky, as You rained them upon the people of Lot").

Abu ʿUbayda said: (the word ﴿أمطر﴾ is used) for punishment; it is said "maṭar" for punishment and "maṭar" for mercy. ﴿أَوِ ائْتِنا بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ ("or bring us a painful punishment"), meaning the very same kind of punishment with which the nations were punished. And concerning this was revealed: ﴿سَأَلَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ واقِعٍ﴾ ("A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall") (Surah al-Maʿarij: 1).

ʿAṭa' said: Indeed, more than ten verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning al-Nadr, and the punishment he asked for befell him on the day of Badr.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of Badr: "Three of the Quraysh who were among you were patient: al-Mut'im ibn ʿAdi, ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith."

Al-Nadr was a captive of al-Miqdad. When the order was given to kill him, al-Miqdad said: "My captive, O Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, he used to say about the Book of Allah what he said." Al-Miqdad said: "My captive, O Messenger of Allah!" He said it three times. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said at the third time: "O Allah, enrich al-Miqdad from Your bounty" [232].

Al-Miqdad said: "This is what I wanted" (Taʾrikh Dimashq: 60/167).

﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنْتَ فِيهِمْ﴾ — The scholars differed concerning the meaning of this verse. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: This is a report about the polytheists; they uttered it, and it is connected to the first verse. It is said that the polytheists used to say: "By Allah, Allah will not punish us while we seek forgiveness, and He does not punish a nation whose prophet is among them." This was part of their speech while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among them. So Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (ﷺ), mentioning to him their ignorance, their delusion, and their seeking victory against themselves when they said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You﴾, and they also said: ﴿It was not for Allah to punish them while you are among them﴾, and ﴿Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. Then He said, as a rebuttal to them: ﴿But why should Allah not punish them while they bar access to al-Masjid al-Haram?﴾, even though you are among them, and even though they were seeking forgiveness.

Others said: This is a new statement, and it is the words of Allah the Exalted speaking about Himself. Then they differed about its meaning and interpretation:

Ibn Abzaʾ, Abu Malik and al-Dahhak said: Its interpretation is: ﴿It was not for Allah to punish them while you are among them﴾, as you remain among them.

They said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was residing in Makka. Then the Prophet departed from among them. A remnant of the Muslims remained there, seeking forgiveness. So Allah revealed after his departure, when those (remaining Muslims) sought forgiveness with it: ﴿Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾.

Then those remaining Muslims also left from among them, and [the polytheists] were punished, and Allah permitted the conquest of Makka. That is the punishment He had promised them.

Ibn ʿAbbas: Those (polytheists) were not punished until the Prophet and the believers had departed from it. Allah said: ﴿It was not for Allah to punish them while you are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, meaning the Muslims. When they departed, Allah said: ﴿But why should Allah not punish them﴾, meaning, He punished them on the day of Badr.

Some of them said: This seeking of forgiveness refers to the polytheists: Allah would not punish these polytheists as long as you were among them, and as long as they were seeking forgiveness. This is because they used to circumambulate the House and say: "Here I am, O Allah, here I am; You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, You possess him and what he possesses," and they said: "Forgiveness, forgiveness." This is the narration of Abu Zumayl from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Abu Musa al-Ashʿari said: Indeed, there was a safeguard for you in it, because of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿It was not for Allah to punish them while you are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾.

As for the Prophet (ﷺ), he has passed away, but the seeking of forgiveness remains until the Day of Resurrection.

Qatada [and Ibn ʿAbbas] and Ibn Yazid said the meaning of ﴿Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ is: if they had sought forgiveness. Al-Hasan said: This verse is abrogated by the verse that follows it: ﴿But why should Allah not punish them…﴾ up to ﴿…for what you used to disbelieve﴾. So they fought in Makka and they suffered hunger and then gained goodness there.

*"Stay, before parting, O Dubaʿa, and let there not be a parting-place of farewell from you."* [[Lisan al-ʿArab: 8/218.]]

I heard someone say: "The mukaʾ was their adhan (call to prayer), and the clapping was their iqama (call to stand for prayer)."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recounted the stories of the earlier generations, al-Nadr said: "If I wished, I could say something like this. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients" ﴿إِنْ هذا إِلَّا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾, which they had in their books.

ʿUthman ibn Maz'un said to him: "Fear Allah, for Muhammad speaks the truth." He said: "I too speak the truth." ʿUthman said: "Muhammad says: there is no god but Allah." He said: "I too say: there is no god but Allah. But this (refers to) the affair of Allah," meaning the idols. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ (Surah al-Zukhruf: 81). Al-Nadr said: "Do you not see that Muhammad has agreed with me in what I say?" meaning his statement ﴿If the Most Merciful had a son﴾.

al-Mughira ibn al-Walid said to him: "By Allah, he did not agree with you, but he says: 'It was not for the Most Merciful to have a son.'"

Al-Nadr grasped this and said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You﴾.

﴿إِنْ كانَ هذا هُوَ الْحَقَّ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ﴾ — ﴿هُوَ﴾ is an ʿimad (the word that stands between two statements, without which the meaning is incomplete; the Basrans call it ḍamīr al-faṣl, the separating pronoun), and it serves as emphasis and a connective in the speech. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾ is in the accusative as the predicate of ﴿كان﴾. ﴿فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ كما أمطرتها على قوم لوط﴾ ("then rain down upon us stones from the sky, as You rained them upon the people of Lot").

Abu ʿUbayda said: (the word ﴿أمطر﴾ is used) for punishment; it is said "maṭar" for punishment and "maṭar" for mercy. ﴿أَوِ ائْتِنا بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ ("or bring us a painful punishment"), meaning the very same kind of punishment with which the nations were punished. And concerning this was revealed: ﴿سَأَلَ سائِلٌ بِعَذابٍ واقِعٍ﴾ ("A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall") (Surah al-Maʿarij: 1).

ʿAṭa' said: Indeed, more than ten verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning al-Nadr, and the punishment he asked for befell him on the day of Badr.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of Badr: "Three of the Quraysh who were among you were patient: al-Mut'im ibn ʿAdi, ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith."

Al-Nadr was a captive of al-Miqdad. When the order was given to kill him, al-Miqdad said: "My captive, O Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, he used to say about the Book of Allah what he said." Al-Miqdad said: "My captive, O Messenger of Allah!" He said it three times. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said at the third time: "O Allah, enrich al-Miqdad from Your bounty" [232].

Al-Miqdad said: "This is what I wanted" (Taʾrikh Dimashq: 60/167).

﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنْتَ فِيهِمْ﴾ — The scholars differed concerning the meaning of this verse. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: This is a report about the polytheists; they uttered it, and it is connected to the first verse. It is said that the polytheists used to say: "By Allah, Allah will not punish us while we seek forgiveness, and He does not punish a nation whose prophet is among them." This was part of their speech while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among them. So Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet (ﷺ), mentioning to him their ignorance, their delusion, and their seeking victory against themselves when they said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You﴾, and they also said: ﴿It was not for Allah to punish them while you are among them﴾, and ﴿Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. Then He said, as a rebuttal to them: ﴿But why should Allah not punish them while they bar access to al-Masjid al-Haram?﴾, even though you are among them, and even though they were seeking forgiveness.

Others said: This is a new statement, and it is the words of Allah the Exalted speaking about Himself. Then they differed about its meaning and interpretation:

Ibn Abzaʾ, Abu Malik and al-Dahhak said: Its interpretation is: ﴿It was not for Allah to punish them while you are among them﴾, as you remain among them.

They said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was residing in Makka. Then the Prophet departed from among them. A remnant of the Muslims remained there, seeking forgiveness. So Allah revealed after his departure, when those (remaining Muslims) sought forgiveness with it: ﴿Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾.

Then those remaining Muslims also left from among them, and [the polytheists] were punished, and Allah permitted the conquest of Makka. That is the punishment He had promised them.

Allah said: ﴿It was not for Allah to punish them while you are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾, meaning the Muslims. When they departed, Allah said: ﴿But why should Allah not punish them﴾, meaning, He punished them on the day of Badr.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 8, verse 36–40:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah.﴾ They spend it so that they may divert people from the religion of Allah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, and Ibn Abza: it was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, who on the day of Uhud hired two thousand from [the Ahabish] to fight the Prophet ﷺ, [in addition to] some individuals from the Arabs. Concerning them Ka'b ibn Malik says:

We came to the middle of the surging sea,
Ahabish among them, some bareheaded and some veiled.

And the Messenger of Allah was among us, whose word we follow,
When he spoke among us a word that does not end.

Three thousand, while we thought them three hundred,
Or if they exceeded, four hundred. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/322, and al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya 4/62, which mentions the remaining verses.]]

Al-Hakam ibn 'Uyayna said: it was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, when he spent on the polytheists on the day of Uhud forty awqiyya, and each awqiyya was forty-two mithqal.

Ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of his narrators: when the Quraysh were struck by the companions of the well on the day of Badr, and Abu Sufyan returned with his camel to Mecca, Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'a, Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl and Safwan ibn Umayya, along with men of Quraysh whose fathers, sons and brothers had been killed on the day of [Badr], approached Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those among the Quraysh who had trade in that caravan, and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, Muhammad has struck you and killed your best men. Help us with this wealth that escaped with his caravan, so that we may hope to obtain vengeance for those of us who were killed." They did so, and Allah revealed this verse concerning them. [['Uyun al-'Ibar: 54, and 'Uyun al-Athar: 1/392.]]

Al-Dahhak said: they are the people of Badr.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning the feeders on the day of Badr, who were twelve men: 'Utba and Shayba, the two sons of Rabi'a ibn 'Abd Shams, and his sons, Munabbih and Nabih, the two sons of al-Hajjaj, al-Bukhturi ibn Hisham, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Hukm ibn Hizam, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Zam'a ibn al-Aswad, al-Harith ibn 'Amir, Nawfal, and al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, all of them from Quraysh; each one of them used to feed ten camels.

Allah said: ﴿So they will spend it, then it will become a regret for them, then they will be overcome,﴾ and will not prevail. ﴿And those who disbelieve, to Hell they will be gathered.﴾ He singled out the disbelievers, on account of those among them who embraced Islam. ﴿That Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good﴾ by that gathering: the disbeliever from the believer, so that Allah admits the believer to the Gardens and the disbeliever to the Fire.

Al-Kalbi said: it means the wicked deed from the good deed, the righteous one; so He rewards righteous deeds with Paradise and rewards wicked deeds with the Fire.

The people of Kufa, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-A'mash and 'Isa recited: ﴿li-yamiza Allahu﴾ with the doubled letter (tashdid).

Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred this.

Ibn Zayd said: it means the good spending in the way of Allah from the wicked spending in the way of Satan, so their expenditures are placed in the depths of Hell, and then it is said to them: "Join them."

Murra al-Hamdani said: it means He distinguishes, in His prior knowledge by which He created them, the believer, whom He created good, from the disbeliever, whom He created wicked in His prior knowledge. That is because they were upon the religion of disbelief, so Allah sent the Messenger with the Book, ﴿that Allah may distinguish the wicked from the good.﴾ Whoever obeys, it becomes evident that he is good, and whoever opposes him, it becomes evident that he is wicked. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/401.]]

﴿And place the wicked one upon another﴾: upon one another, one heap above another, ﴿and pile them all together﴾, that is, gather them until He makes them like a towering cloud, which is the dense gathered mass, ﴿and place them in Hell.﴾ The report about them is in the singular because of the singular word of Allah ﴿that Allah may distinguish the wicked﴾; then He says ﴿those are the losers,﴾ in the plural, returning to the beginning of the report, meaning His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth…those are the losers﴾, those whose transaction profited and whose trade was lost, because they purchased with their wealth the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/325.]]

﴿Say to those who disbelieve﴾, meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions: ﴿if they desist, they will be forgiven what has already passed﴾, if they desist from shirk. Muhammad said: ﴿they will be forgiven what has already passed﴾ of their deeds before Islam. ﴿But if they return﴾ to fight Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿then the precedent of the former peoples has already passed﴾, regarding the victory of the prophets and the allies and the destruction of the disbelievers and enemies, like the day of Badr.

The Ustadh, the Imam Abu Ishaq said: I heard al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan say: I heard my father say: I heard 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Warraq say: I heard Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi say: "Indeed, I hope that the Tawhid which was not unable to demolish the disbelief that preceded it is not unable to demolish the sin that follows it."

Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi recited to me on this: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Zaydi recited to me:

The youth deserves pardon when he confesses,
Then he ceases from what he committed and did.

Due to His saying, regarding those who confess: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, they will be forgiven what has already passed.﴾

... ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah﴾, meaning shirk. Abu al-'Aliya said: trial. al-Rabi' said: until no believer is tempted away from his religion. ﴿And religion is entirely for Allah﴾: pure monotheism, with no shirk in it, and discarding whatever is worshipped besides Him as rivals.

Qatada said: until it is said, "There is no god but Allah," for which the Prophet of Allah fought and to which he called.

It was also said: until obedience and worship are purely for Allah, to the exclusion of anyone else. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 2/262.]] ﴿And if they desist﴾ from disbelief and fighting, ﴿then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ ﴿But if they turn away﴾ from faith and return, then its people said: ﴿know that Allah is your Protector﴾, your Helper and Supporter, ﴿an excellent Protector and an excellent Helper.﴾

Regarding (حَيَّ) there are two readings. The people of Medina read (حيي) with two yas, like (خشيي) in (على الإيمان). The rest read (حَيَّ) with one shaddated ya, through idgham (assimilation), because it is written in the Book with a single ya. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

﴿When Allah showed them to you in your dream, [O Muhammad], as few.﴾ That is, the polytheists. ﴿In your dream﴾, meaning in your sleep. It was said: "in the place of your sleep", meaning your eye. ﴿And had He shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage and disputed over the matter.﴾ That is, you would have become cowardly and disagreed about the affair. Allah, the Exalted, showed them to him in his dream as few, and he (ﷺ) informed them of this. It was therefore a source of reassurance for them and a blessing from Allah upon them, by which He encouraged them against their enemy. This is the meaning of His words, ﴿but Allah saved [you]﴾. Ibn Abbas said: Allah saved their affair when He gave them victory over their enemy. ﴿And when He showed them to you as few when you met, and He made them appear few in your eyes﴾.

Muqatil said: That is because the Prophet (ﷺ) saw in a dream that the enemy was few before the encounter with the enemy, so the Prophet (ﷺ) informed his companions of what he had seen. They said: "The Prophet's dream is true; the people are few." When they met at Badr, Allah made the polytheists appear few in the eyes of the believers, and the Prophet's (ﷺ) dream was confirmed.

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: On the day of Badr they appeared so few in our eyes that I said to a man beside me: "[We see them as seventy]." He said: "I see them as a hundred." Then we captured a man and asked him, "How many were you?" He said: "A thousand." ﴿And He made you appear few in their eyes﴾, O assembly of believers.

Al-Suddi said: Some of the polytheists said: "The caravan has turned back, so return." Abu Jahl said: "Now, when Muhammad and his companions [come down upon you], do not turn back until you have annihilated them. Do not kill them with weapons; seize them alive, so that Allah is not worshipped after today. Muhammad and his companions are merely a mouthful of meat; so bind them with ropes."

[This is] like His saying, from His power over Himself.

Al-Kalbi said: The believers considered the polytheists few, and the believers [considered] the believers [few], al-Bahtari: [some] against [others].

﴿That Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾, existing in His knowledge: the support of Islam and its people, and the humiliation of polytheism and its people.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: ﴿That Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾, by exacting vengeance upon His enemies and bestowing favour upon His allies. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 8, verses 45–51:**

﴿O you who believe, when you meet a company (fi'ah), that is, a disbelieving band, stand firm (fa-uthbutu) to fight them, and do not turn your backs. Remember Allah much (dhikran kathiran), that is, call upon Allah for victory over them and triumph against them.﴾ Qatadah said: Allah commanded them to remember Him at the moment they are most burdened by the striking of swords. ﴿So that you may prosper (tuflihun)﴾, that is, succeed with victory and triumph. ﴿Obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute (tanazu'u), lest you lose heart (fatafshalu)﴾, that is, you lose and become weak.

Al-Hasan said: "fatafshilu" with a kasra on the shin. ﴿And your strength (rihukum) will depart﴾. Mujahid said: your victory. The "rih" of the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) departed when they disputed with him on the day of Uhud. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/21.]]

Al-Suddi said: your community, your unity. Muqatil said: your life. Ata said: your boldness. Yaman said: your dominance. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: your power. Al-Akhfash said: your state (dawlatukum). Ibn Zayd said: it is the wind of victory. No victory has ever come except by a wind that Allah sends against the faces of the enemy. When that wind is withdrawn, they have no stability. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I was made victorious by the eastern wind (al-saba), and ʿAd was destroyed by the western wind (al-dabur)." [236] [[Musnad Ahmad: 1/228; Sahih al-Bukhari: 2/22.]]

It is said of a man when the world turns toward him in what he desires: "The wind today is for so-and-so."

ʿUbayd ibn al-Abras said:

*As we protected you on the day of al-Naʿf from Shutab,*
*and superiority belonged to the people by wind and by numbers.* [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/21; Mu'jam al-Buldan: 3/343.]]

And another poet said:

*O my two companions, no one is left in the valley*
*except ʿUbayd and Umm Bayn with the camels.*

*Will you two wait a little, waiting for their heedlessness,*
*or will you run, for the wind is for the one who runs?* [[Al-Sihah: 1/368; the verse is by Imru' al-Qays in his Mu'allaqah.]]

Abu al-Qasim, the aforementioned, recited to me, saying: Abu Nasr ibn Mansur al-Karaji, the scribe, recited to me:

*When your winds blow, seize them,*
*for every fluttering thing has a stillness.*

*Do not be heedless of doing good during them,*
*for you do not know when the stillness will come.* [[Taj al-ʿArus: 2/149; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/384.]]

Allah's words: ﴿And be patient; indeed Allah is with the patient. And do not be like those who went forth from their homes boastfully (bataran), showing off, and who bar from the way of Allah﴾ — "wa yasuddun" is coordinated with "bataran wa ri'a'a al-nas" (boastfully and to be seen by people), and its meaning is "they look and see," since a future verb is not coordinated with a past one. ﴿And Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾

These were the people of Makkah who went out on the day of Badr, with insolence and boasting. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, Quraysh has come with its pride and its arrogance, opposing You and Your Messenger." [237] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/24.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When Abu Sufyan saw that he had secured his caravan, he sent to Quraysh: "You went out to protect your property, and now Allah has saved it, so return." He then met the caravan in which Abu Sufyan was, so that they would order Quraysh to return to Makkah. He said to them: "Turn back." Abu Jahl said: "By Allah, we will not turn back until we reach Badr." Badr was a seasonal gathering of the Arabs, where a market was held every year. We would stay there three days, slaughter camels, feed people, serve wine, play music on instruments, with singing girls (al-qiyan), and the Arabs would hear of it, and they would always hold us in awe. They arrived there, and they were given cups of death instead of wine, and the mourning women wailed over them instead of the singing girls. [[Zad al-Masir: 3/249.]]

Allah forbade His believing servants from being like them, and commanded them to sincerity of intention, fear (of Allah) in supporting His religion, and aiding the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them﴾ — the adornment was, as said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Ishaq, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and others: When Quraysh resolved to march, they recalled the war between them and the Bani Bakr ibn ʿAbd Manaf ibn Kinanah, and the war between them and the Bani Bakr ibn ʿAbd Manat ibn Kinanah. This was what would keep them firm. Iblis came in an army of devils with him, and appeared in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Juʿshum, the poet of Kinanah, who was one of the nobles of Kinanah. [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 4/477.]]

The poet said:

*O you who wrong me, how do you intend to take my right?*
*And Allah is free of every mishap.*

﴿When the two hosts sighted each other﴾, that is, the two groups met, and Iblis saw the angels descending from heaven, and knew he had no power against them, ﴿he turned back on his heels (nakasa ʿala ʿaqibayhi)﴾. Al-Dahhak said: he turned and fled. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: he went backward on his back, fleeing. Qutrub and Aban ibn Thaʿlabah said: he returned from where he came.

The poet said:

*You turned back on your heels on the day you came,*
*while hoping for the spoils of the mighty, thundering army.*

ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawahah said: "When you saw the Messenger of Allah, you turned back on your heels, fleeing."

Al-Kalbi said: When they met, Iblis was in the ranks of the polytheists in the form of Suraqah ibn Kinanah, holding the hand of al-Harith ibn Hisham. ﴿He turned back on his heels﴾, and al-Harith said to him: "O Suraqah, where are you going? Will you abandon us in this state?"

He said: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see﴾. He said: "By Allah, we see nothing but the spies of Yathrib." He said: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah.﴾

Al-Harith said: "Why was this not yesterday?" Then he pushed al-Harith in the chest, and he went away, and the people fled. When they arrived in Makkah, they said: "Suraqah defeated the people." This reached Suraqah, and he said: "It has reached me that you are saying I defeated the people. By Allah, I did not know until your defeat reached me." They said: "Did you not come to us on such-and-such a day?" He swore to them. When they repented, they knew that it had been Satan.

Al-Hasan said concerning His words ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see﴾: Iblis came to Jibril, wrapped in a turban and a cloak, walking before the Prophet (ﷺ), and in his hand was a bridle, leading a horse which he did not ride.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-ʿAnbari say: I heard Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Bushanji say: "The most boastful line of verse said in Islam is the saying of Baghid al-Ansari on the day of Badr:

*And at the well of Badr, when we turned back their faces,*
*Jibril was beneath our banner, and Muhammad.*" [[See al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah by Ibn Kathir: 1/391, where it is attributed to Hassan ibn Thabit. Al-Bakri al-Andalusi attributed it to Kaʿb ibn Malik; see Mu'jam ma Ista'jam: 1/232.]]

Qatadah and Ibn Ishaq said: Iblis said: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see﴾, and he spoke the truth about his enemy. And he said: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾, and the enemy of Allah lied. By Allah, there was no fear of Allah in him, but he knew that they had no strength and no protection, so he supported them and then abandoned them. This is the habit of the enemy of Allah with whoever obeys him: when truth and falsehood meet, he abandons them and disowns them.

Ata said: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾ — that He would destroy me along with those who are destroyed. Al-Kalbi said: He feared that Jibril would seize him and inform them of his condition, so they would not obey him afterward. And it was said that its meaning is: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾, that is, I know the truth of His promise to His friends, for he was certain of his affair.

Al-Ustadh al-Imam Abu Ishaq said: I saw in some tafsirs: "Indeed, I fear Allah concerning you," and "Allah is severe in punishment." Some said: this is a report about Iblis. Others said: the speech ends at His words ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾, and Allah said: ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Ibrahim ibn Abi ʿAblah narrated from Talhah ibn ʿUbayd Allah ibn Kuraiz that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Satan was never seen on any day more humiliated, more repelled, more despised, or more enraged than on the Day of ʿArafah, and that is only because of what he saw of the descent of mercy and Allah's forgiveness of great sins. Except what he saw on the Day of Badr." [238] He saw Jibril, who was driving the angels. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/419; Tarikh Dimashq: 43/539; Muwatta' Malik: 1/422, no. 245.]]

﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease (doubt and hypocrisy) say: "Their religion has deceived these (people)"﴾ — meaning the believers: "These are people in Makkah who were oppressed, whom their fathers and relatives had held back from emigrating. When Quraysh went out to Badr, they compelled them to go unwillingly. When they saw the Muslims' small number, they doubted and apostatized, and said: 'Their religion has deceived these.'" Then all of them were killed among the disbelievers: Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, Abu Qays ibn al-Fakih ibn al-Mughirah, both of al-Makhzum; al-Harith ibn Zamʿah ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib; ʿAli ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf; al-ʿAs ibn Munabbih ibn al-Hajjaj; al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah; and ʿAmr ibn Umayyah. When they were killed with the polytheists, the angels struck their faces and their backs. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you could see, O Muhammad, when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved (yatawaffa), that is, seize their spirits at Badr, striking their faces and their backs (adbarahum)﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: it means their rear ends, but Allah, being generous, uses euphemism.

Muhammad ibn Yazid? — no; instead: Murrah al-Hamdhani and Ibn Jurayj said: "their faces" means what faces them, and "their backs" means what turns away from them, and the sense is: they strike their whole bodies. Ibn ʿAbbas said: when the polytheists advanced toward the Muslims with their faces, they were struck on their faces with swords, and when they turned away, the angels overtook them and struck their backs.

Al-Hasan said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw between the shoulders of a man something like a sandal-strap." He said: "That is the striking of the angels."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: striking the face is punishment for their disbelief, and striking the back is punishment for their sins.

﴿And taste (dhuqu)﴾ — there is an implied element here: that is, they say to them: taste ﴿the punishment of the burning﴾ in the Hereafter. I saw in some tafsirs: with the angels were iron maces, and whenever they struck, the fire flared in the wounds, and that is His saying: ﴿taste the punishment of the burning.﴾ The meaning of "dhuqu" is: experience and endure. The poet said:

*So taste as we tasted on the morning of Muhajjar,*
*from rage in our livers and anguish.* [[The verse is by Tufayl al-Ghanawi, as in Lisan al-ʿArab: 1/339.]]

It is also permissible that "dhuqu" means the place of trial and testing. The Arabs say: "Ride this horse and test it (fadhuqhu)," and "Look at so-and-so and test what he has." Al-Shammakh said describing a bow:

*It tasted and gave it a portion of softness,*

*for every fluttering thing has a stillness.*

*O you who wrong me, how do you intend to take my right?*
*And Allah is free of every mishap.*

Al-Dahhak said: he turned and fled. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: he went backward on his back, fleeing. Qutrub and Aban ibn Thaʿlabah said: he returned from where he came.

*You turned back on your heels on the day you came,*
*while hoping for the spoils of the mighty, thundering army.*

ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawahah said: "When you saw the Messenger of Allah, you turned back on your heels, fleeing."

Al-Harith said: "Why was this not yesterday?" Then he pushed al-Harith in the chest, and he went away, and the people fled. When they arrived in Makkah, they said: "Suraqah defeated the people." Ata said: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾ — that He would destroy me along with those who are destroyed. ʿUbayd ibn al-Abras said:

*As we protected you on the day of al-Naʿf from Shutab,*
*and superiority belonged to the people by wind and by numbers.* [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/21; Mu'jam al-Buldan: 3/343.]]

And another poet said:

*O my two companions, no one is left in the valley*
*except ʿUbayd and Umm Bayn with the camels.*

*Will you two wait a little, waiting for their heedlessness,*
*or will you run, for the wind is for the one who runs?* [[Al-Sihah: 1/368; the verse is by Imru' al-Qays in his Mu'allaqah.]]

Abu al-Qasim, the aforementioned, recited to me, saying: Abu Nasr ibn Mansur al-Karaji, the scribe, recited to me:

*When your winds blow, seize them,*
*for every fluttering thing has a stillness.*

*Do not be heedless of doing good during them,*
*for you do not know when the stillness will come.* [[Taj al-ʿArus: 2/149; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/384.]]

Allah's words: ﴿And be patient; indeed Allah is with the patient. And do not be like those who went forth from their homes boastfully (bataran), showing off, and who bar from the way of Allah﴾ — "wa yasuddun" is coordinated with "bataran wa ri'a'a al-nas" (boastfully and to be seen by people), and its meaning is "they look and see," since a future verb is not coordinated with a past one. ﴿And Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾

These were the people of Makkah who went out on the day of Badr, with insolence and boasting. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, Quraysh has come with its pride and its arrogance, opposing You and Your Messenger." [237] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/24.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When Abu Sufyan saw that he had secured his caravan, he sent to Quraysh: "You went out to protect your property, and now Allah has saved it, so return." He then met the caravan in which Abu Sufyan was, so that they would order Quraysh to return to Makkah. He said to them: "Turn back." Abu Jahl said: "By Allah, we will not turn back until we reach Badr." Badr was a seasonal gathering of the Arabs, where a market was held every year. We would stay there three days, slaughter camels, feed people, serve wine, play music on instruments, with singing girls (al-qiyan), and the Arabs would hear of it, and they would always hold us in awe. They arrived there, and they were given cups of death instead of wine, and the mourning women wailed over them instead of the singing girls. [[Zad al-Masir: 3/249.]]

Allah forbade His believing servants from being like them, and commanded them to sincerity of intention, fear (of Allah) in supporting His religion, and aiding the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them﴾ — the adornment was, as said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Ishaq, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and others: When Quraysh resolved to march, they recalled the war between them and the Bani Bakr ibn ʿAbd Manaf ibn Kinanah, and the war between them and the Bani Bakr ibn ʿAbd Manat ibn Kinanah. This was what would keep them firm. Iblis came in an army of devils with him, and appeared in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Juʿshum, the poet of Kinanah, who was one of the nobles of Kinanah. [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 4/477.]]

The poet said:

*O you who wrong me, how do you intend to take my right?*
*And Allah is free of every mishap.*

﴿When the two hosts sighted each other﴾, that is, the two groups met, and Iblis saw the angels descending from heaven, and knew he had no power against them, ﴿he turned back on his heels (nakasa ʿala ʿaqibayhi)﴾. Al-Dahhak said: he turned and fled. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: he went backward on his back, fleeing. Qutrub and Aban ibn Thaʿlabah said: he returned from where he came.

The poet said:

*You turned back on your heels on the day you came,*
*while hoping for the spoils of the mighty, thundering army.*

ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawahah said: "When you saw the Messenger of Allah, you turned back on your heels, fleeing."

Al-Kalbi said: When they met, Iblis was in the ranks of the polytheists in the form of Suraqah ibn Kinanah, holding the hand of al-Harith ibn Hisham. ﴿He turned back on his heels﴾, and al-Harith said to him: "O Suraqah, where are you going? Will you abandon us in this state?"

He said: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see﴾. He said: "By Allah, we see nothing but the spies of Yathrib." He said: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah.﴾

Al-Harith said: "Why was this not yesterday?" Then he pushed al-Harith in the chest, and he went away, and the people fled. When they arrived in Makkah, they said: "Suraqah defeated the people." This reached Suraqah, and he said: "It has reached me that you are saying I defeated the people. By Allah, I did not know until your defeat reached me." They said: "Did you not come to us on such-and-such a day?" He swore to them. When they repented, they knew that it had been Satan.

Al-Hasan said concerning His words ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see﴾: Iblis came to Jibril, wrapped in a turban and a cloak, walking before the Prophet (ﷺ), and in his hand was a bridle, leading a horse which he did not ride.

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Abu Zakariyya al-ʿAnbari say: I heard Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Bushanji say: "The most boastful line of verse said in Islam is the saying of Baghid al-Ansari on the day of Badr:

*And at the well of Badr, when we turned back their faces,*
*Jibril was beneath our banner, and Muhammad.*" [[See al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah by Ibn Kathir: 1/391, where it is attributed to Hassan ibn Thabit. Al-Bakri al-Andalusi attributed it to Kaʿb ibn Malik; see Mu'jam ma Ista'jam: 1/232.]]

Qatadah and Ibn Ishaq said: Iblis said: ﴿Indeed, I see what you do not see﴾, and he spoke the truth about his enemy. And he said: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾, and the enemy of Allah lied. By Allah, there was no fear of Allah in him, but he knew that they had no strength and no protection, so he supported them and then abandoned them. This is the habit of the enemy of Allah with whoever obeys him: when truth and falsehood meet, he abandons them and disowns them.

Ata said: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾ — that He would destroy me along with those who are destroyed. Al-Kalbi said: He feared that Jibril would seize him and inform them of his condition, so they would not obey him afterward. And it was said that its meaning is: ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾, that is, I know the truth of His promise to His friends, for he was certain of his affair.

Al-Ustadh al-Imam Abu Ishaq said: I saw in some tafsirs: "Indeed, I fear Allah concerning you," and "Allah is severe in punishment." Some said: this is a report about Iblis. Others said: the speech ends at His words ﴿Indeed, I fear Allah﴾, and Allah said: ﴿And Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Ibrahim ibn Abi ʿAblah narrated from Talhah ibn ʿUbayd Allah ibn Kuraiz that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Satan was never seen on any day more humiliated, more repelled, more despised, or more enraged than on the Day of ʿArafah, and that is only because of what he saw of the descent of mercy and Allah's forgiveness of great sins. Except what he saw on the Day of Badr." [238] He saw Jibril, who was driving the angels. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 2/419; Tarikh Dimashq: 43/539; Muwatta' Malik: 1/422, no. 245.]]

﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease (doubt and hypocrisy) say: "Their religion has deceived these (people)"﴾ — meaning the believers: "These are people in Makkah who were oppressed, whom their fathers and relatives had held back from emigrating. When Quraysh went out to Badr, they compelled them to go unwillingly. When they saw the Muslims' small number, they doubted and apostatized, and said: 'Their religion has deceived these.'" Then all of them were killed among the disbelievers: Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, Abu Qays ibn al-Fakih ibn al-Mughirah, both of al-Makhzum; al-Harith ibn Zamʿah ibn al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib; ʿAli ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf; al-ʿAs ibn Munabbih ibn al-Hajjaj; al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah; and ʿAmr ibn Umayyah. When they were killed with the polytheists, the angels struck their faces and their backs. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you could see, O Muhammad, when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved (yatawaffa), that is, seize their spirits at Badr, striking their faces and their backs (adbarahum)﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: it means their rear ends, but Allah, being generous, uses euphemism.

Muhammad ibn Yazid? — no; instead: Murrah al-Hamdhani and Ibn Jurayj said: "their faces" means what faces them, and "their backs" means what turns away from them, and the sense is: they strike their whole bodies. Ibn ʿAbbas said: when the polytheists advanced toward the Muslims with their faces, they were struck on their faces with swords, and when they turned away, the angels overtook them and struck their backs.

Al-Hasan said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I saw between the shoulders of a man something like a sandal-strap." He said: "That is the striking of the angels."

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: striking the face is punishment for their disbelief, and striking the back is punishment for their sins.

﴿And taste (dhuqu)﴾ — there is an implied element here: that is, they say to them: taste ﴿the punishment of the burning﴾ in the Hereafter. I saw in some tafsirs: with the angels were iron maces, and whenever they struck, the fire flared in the wounds, and that is His saying: ﴿taste the punishment of the burning.﴾ The meaning of "dhuqu" is: experience and endure. The poet said:

*So taste as we tasted on the morning of Muhajjar,*
*from rage in our livers and anguish.* [[The verse is by Tufayl al-Ghanawi, as in Lisan al-ʿArab: 1/339.]]

It is also permissible that "dhuqu" means the place of trial and testing. The Arabs say: "Ride this horse and test it (fadhuqhu)," and "Look at so-and-so and test what he has." Al-Shammakh said describing a bow:

*It tasted and gave it a portion of softness,*
*enough, and a barrier to stop the arrow from passing through.* [[Lisan al-ʿArab: 10/112, where it reads "al-nil hajiz."]]

Its origin is tasting with the mouth.

﴿That is for what your hands have sent forward﴾, that is, what you earned and did. ﴿And that Allah is not unjust to the servants﴾ — He takes them without any reduction. In the position of "anna" there are two grammatical (i'rab) possibilities: first, the accusative, coordinated with "bima qaddamat" (for what they sent forward), the meaning being: "and that Allah"; second, the nominative, coordinated with "dhalika" (that), the meaning being: "and that is because Allah..."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 8, verses 45–51:**

﴿O you who believe, when you meet a company (fi'ah), that is, a disbelieving band, stand firm (fa-uthbutu) to fight them, and do not turn your backs. Remember Allah much (dhikran kathiran), that is, call upon Allah for victory over them and triumph against them.﴾ Qatadah said: Allah commanded them to remember Him at the moment they are most burdened by the striking of swords. ﴿So that you may prosper (tuflihun)﴾, that is, succeed with victory and triumph. ﴿Obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute (tanazu'u), lest you lose heart (fatafshalu)﴾, that is, you lose and become weak.

Al-Hasan said: "fatafshilu" with a kasra on the shin. ﴿And your strength (rihukum) will depart﴾. Mujahid said: your victory. The "rih" of the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) departed when they disputed with him on the day of Uhud. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/21.]]

Al-Suddi said: your community, your unity. Muqatil said: your life. Ata said: your boldness. Yaman said: your dominance. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: your power. Al-Akhfash said: your state (dawlatukum). Ibn Zayd said: it is the wind of victory. No victory has ever come except by a wind that Allah sends against the faces of the enemy. When that wind is withdrawn, they have no stability. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I was made victorious by the eastern wind (al-saba), and ʿAd was destroyed by the western wind (al-dabur)." Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 8, verse 52–60:

Like the custom of the family of Pharaoh (ka-da'b Al Fir'awn). Ibn 'Abbas said: like the deed of the family of Pharaoh. Al-Dahhak said: like their practice. Mujahid and 'Ata' said: like their way (sunnah). Yaman said: like their example, meaning that the people of Badr acted like the family of Pharaoh in disbelief and sins, so God dealt with them as He dealt with the family of Pharaoh, with destruction and punishment. Al-Kisa'i said: just as the family of Pharaoh denied as you denied, and disbelieved as you disbelieved. Al-Akhfash, al-Mu'arrikh and Abu 'Ubayda said:

Like the habit of the family of Pharaoh.

﴿And those before them disbelieved in the signs of God, so God seized them for their sins.﴾ That is, God punished them for their sins. ﴿Indeed God is strong and severe in punishment.﴾ ﴿That is because God would never change a blessing He had bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves.﴾

Al-Kalbi said: this refers to the people of Makkah. ﴿He fed them against hunger and secured them against fear﴾, and sent Muhammad (peace be upon him) to them, but they changed the blessings of God. Their changing them was that they disbelieved in them and abandoned gratitude for them. Al-Suddi said: the blessing of God is Muhammad ﷺ, whom He bestowed upon Quraysh, but they denied him and disbelieved in him, so He transferred it to the Ansar.

﴿And that God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿Like the custom of the family of Pharaoh and those before them﴾, from the disbelieving nations, ﴿who denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins﴾: some with the quake, some with the sinking into the earth, some with transformation into apes and swine, some with stones, and some with water. Likewise We destroyed the disbelievers of Makkah with the sword and humiliation. ﴿And We drowned the family of Pharaoh, and all of them were wrongdoers.﴾ The verse ﴿Those with whom you made a covenant﴾.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Bakr 'Abdash say: "Min" here is a connective particle (silah) for "alladhina 'ahadta" (those whom you made a covenant with). I also heard him say: I heard al-Munhal ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Ash'ath say: "Dakhalat bayna" because the meaning is: those from whom you took the covenant. It was also said: "'Ahadta minhum" meaning "ma'hum" (with them). ﴿Then they break their covenant every time﴾, and they are the Banu Qurayzah, who broke the covenant that existed between them and the Messenger of God ﷺ, and they aided the polytheists of Makkah with weapons against the Prophet ﷺ and his companions. Then they said: "We forgot and erred." Then he made a covenant with them a second time, and they broke it and sided with the disbelievers against the Messenger of God on the day of the Trench. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf wrote to Makkah agreeing with them to oppose the Messenger of God ﷺ. ﴿And they do not fear﴾, that is, they do not fear God in breaking the covenant.

﴿So if you encounter them in war﴾, that is, you see them and find them in war, ﴿then scatter those behind them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: then punish those behind them. It was also said: disperse every breaker of covenants who reaches the level of these people. 'Ata' said: inflict heavy slaughter upon them until others, from the people of Makkah and Yemen, fear you. Ibn Kaysan said: kill them, so that none who come after them flee from you.

"I wander through the valleys every day, fearing that a wise man might scatter me."

Like the habit of the family of Pharaoh.

Al-Suddi said: the blessing of God is Muhammad ﷺ, whom He bestowed upon Quraysh, but they denied him and disbelieved in him, so He transferred it to the Ansar.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 8, verse 61–67:

وَإِنْ جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فَاجْنَحْ لَها [And if they incline to peace, then incline to it] — meaning: go over to it and make peace with them. They said: this was before (Bara'a), then it was abrogated (mansukh) by His saying: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, and His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah﴾, the verse. ﴿And put your trust in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾ — that is, they will betray and scheme against you. Mujahid said: this refers to Qurayza. ﴿Then sufficient for you is Allah﴾ — He will suffice you. ﴿It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers.﴾ al-Suddi said: this refers to the Ansar. ﴿And He brought their hearts together﴾ — He joined their hearts upon His religion after years of war, so He made them all one after they had been scattered, and brothers after they had been enemies. ﴿Even if you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have brought their hearts together, but Allah brought them together. Indeed, He is Exalted in Might, Wise﴾ — up to His saying, the Exalted, "the Wise."

Ibn ʿAffan narrated from ʿUmayr ibn Ishaq, who said: "We used to say that the first thing to be lifted from people is harmony (al-ulfah)." ﴿O Prophet, sufficient for you is Allah﴾.

[ ... ] [[An unreadable word.]]

Abu al-Mughira narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: "There embraced Islam with the Prophet ﷺ thirty-three men and six women. Then ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) embraced Islam, and this verse was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, sufficient for you is Allah and for those who follow you﴾."

Most exegetes said: the place of "man" (مَنِ) is in the accusative, as a conjunction with the kaf in His saying "ḥasbuka" (sufficient for you), and the meaning of the verse is: sufficient for you and for those who follow you. Some of them said it is in the nominative, as a conjunction with the name of Allah, its sense being: "Sufficient for you is Allah and those of the believers who follow you."

﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight﴾ — exhort them to combat. ﴿If there are twenty among you who are steadfast, they will overcome two hundred﴾ of their enemy and subdue them. ﴿And if there are a hundred among you who are steadfast, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.﴾ This is because the polytheists are a people who fight without seeking reward or hoping for recompense, so they do not stand firm when you engage them in battle, out of fear of being killed. The form of the verse is a report, but its meaning is a command.

This was on the day of Badr: one man of the believers was pitted against ten of the disbelievers, so the believers found it burdensome and cried out, and Allah, the Generous, lightened it for them and revealed: ﴿Now Allah has lightened it for you, and He knows that among you there is weakness.﴾ That is, in one man against fighting ten, and a hundred against fighting a thousand. Abu Jaʿfar read ḍaʿfan with a fatḥa on the ḍad; some read ḍuʿafāʾ with a long vowel, as the plural of ḍaʿīf, like shurakāʾ.

﴿So if there are a hundred steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred of the disbelievers; and if there are a thousand among you, they will overcome two thousand by the permission of Allah. And Allah is with the steadfast.﴾ [That is: twenty out of ten are like two out of one, so the first twenty is broken as two is broken.] [[Addition from Tafsir al-Qurtubi 8/44; the manuscript is damaged.]] And when they are at half the strength of their enemy, it is not fitting for them to flee from them; and if they are fewer than that, fighting is not obligatory upon them, and it is permissible for them to withdraw from them. [[Correction of the wording from Tafsir al-Tabari 10/50; the manuscript is damaged.]]

﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives until he has inflicted slaughter upon the land.﴾

Al-Aʿmash narrated from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Abu ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: "When the day of Badr came, the captives were brought, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'What do you say about these?'"

Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are your people and your family. Spare them and seek their help; perhaps Allah will turn to them in mercy. And take from them a ransom, which will give us strength against the disbelievers."

ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of Allah, they denied you and expelled you; so strike their necks. Enable me to strike the neck of ʿAqil, and enable me to [strike] so-and-so, a relative of ʿUmar. Strike his neck, for these are the leaders of disbelief." ʿAbd Allah ibn Rawaha said: "O Messenger of Allah, look for a valley abundant in firewood, lead them into it, and then set it alight upon them with fire." Al-ʿAbbas said: "You have severed your ties of kinship." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent and did not answer them. Then he entered, and some people said: "He will take the saying of Abu Bakr"; some said: "He will take the saying of ʿUmar"; and some said: "He will take the saying of Ibn Rawaha."

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and said: "Indeed Allah softens the hearts of men until they are softer than milk, and Allah hardens the hearts of men until they are harder than stones. Your likeness, O Abu Bakr, is that of Abraham, who said: ﴿Whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾. And your likeness, O Abu Bakr, is that of Jesus, who said: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾. Your likeness, O ʿUmar, is that of Noah, who said: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant﴾. And your likeness is that of Moses, who said: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts﴾ [[Surah Yunus: 88.]] the verse."

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You are today in need, so let none of you escape except by ransom or by the striking of a neck." ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud said: "Except Suhayl ibn al-Bayda, for I heard him mention Islam." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell silent. He said: "I never saw myself on a day more fearful that stones would fall upon me from the sky than that day, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Except Suhayl ibn al-Bayda.'" [[See: Musnad Ahmad 1/384; and Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari 10/57.]]

He said: "When it was the next day, I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found him and Abu Bakr sitting and weeping. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me, what is it that makes you and your companion weep? If I find weeping, I will weep, and if I do not find it, I will pretend to weep.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'I weep for what was presented to your companions regarding their taking of ransom. Indeed, your punishment was presented to me, and it came as near as this tree, which is close to the Prophet of Allah.' Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not for a Prophet to have captives…﴾"

(Read with the ta' by Basri; the rest read with the ya'.) Asra is the plural of asir, like qatil and qatla. ﴿Until he has inflicted slaughter upon the land﴾ — that is, until he has thoroughly killed, captured and subdued the polytheists. One says "athkhana fulan fi hadha al-amr," meaning he went to the extreme; and "athkhantuhu ma'rifa," meaning I made him ma'rifa (overcome), in the sense of I subdued him.

Qatada said: "This is the day of Badr. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ransomed them for four thousand each. By my life, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not yet inflicted slaughter that day, and it was the first battle in which he fought the polytheists."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "This was on the day of Badr, when the Muslims were few. When they increased and their authority grew strong, Allah, the Exalted, revealed after this concerning the captives: ﴿Then either release them as a favour or take ransom﴾. So Allah made His Prophet and the believers free in the matter of the captives: if they wished, they could kill them; if they wished, they could enslave them; if they wished, they could ransom them; and if they wished, they could show them mercy."

﴿You desire the goods of this world﴾, O believers, by taking ransom. ﴿But Allah desires the reward of the Hereafter﴾ by your subduing the polytheists and supporting the religion of Allah. ﴿And Allah is Exalted in Might, Wise.﴾

Al-Aʿmash narrated from ʿAmr ibn Murra, from Abu ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, who said: "When the day of Badr came, the captives were brought, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'What do you say about these?'"

Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are your people and your family. Spare them and seek their help; perhaps Allah will turn to them in mercy. And take from them a ransom, which will give us strength against the disbelievers."

ʿUmar said: "O Messenger of Allah, they denied you and expelled you; so strike their necks. Enable me to strike the neck of ʿAqil, and enable me to [strike] so-and-so, a relative of ʿUmar. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fell silent. He said: "I never saw myself on a day more fearful that stones would fall upon me from the sky than that day, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Except Suhayl ibn al-Bayda.'" Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 8, verse 68–75:

﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾ the verse. Ibn 'Abbas said: Spoils of war were forbidden before the Prophet ﷺ was sent, to the prophets and all the nations. Whenever they obtained booty, they would offer it to the fire [in the manuscript: "to the Qur'an"], and it was forbidden for them to take any of it, little or much. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had written in the Mother of the Book that spoils and captives were lawful for Muhammad and his community. When the day of Badr came, the believers hastened to take the spoils, so Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾, meaning: had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded for you, O people of Badr, in the Preserved Tablet, that Allah the Exalted has made the booty lawful for you.

al-Hasan, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾ means that He would not punish anyone who witnessed Badr with the Prophet ﷺ. And [it means]: had there not been a decree that preceded, that He would forgive minor sins for those who avoid major sins. Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿Had there not been a decree from Allah that preceded﴾ means that He does not lead astray a people after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should guard against, and that He does not seize a people who did something in ignorance, ﴿surely a great punishment would have touched you﴾, meaning: would have reached and struck you, ﴿for what you took﴾ of the spoils and the ransom ﴿before it was commanded to you﴾.

Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated from 'Ubaydah al-Salmani, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions regarding the captives of Badr: "If you wish, you may kill them, and if you wish, you may take ransom for them, and [in that case] a number equal to them of you will be martyred." The captives numbered seventy. They said: "Rather, we will take the ransom, benefit from it, and gain strength against our enemy, and a number equal to them of us will be martyred." 'Ubaydah said: They chose both good options, and so seventy of them were killed at Uhud.

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Zayd said: None of the believers who were present had any inclination except toward the spoils, except 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who kept striking the neck of every captive he met, and he said to the Messenger of Allah: "What have we to do with the spoils! We are a people who strive in the religion of Allah until Allah is worshipped." He advised the Messenger of Allah to kill the captives. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of Allah, excessive slaughter in killing is dearer to me than sparing the men." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Had a punishment come down from the heavens, none would have been saved from it except 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh."

Then Allah said: ﴿So eat of what you have taken as lawful and good, and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Hammam ibn Munabbih said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from Muhammad, who said ﷺ: "Spoils were not made lawful for those before us." That is because Allah saw our weakness and incapacity, so He made them good for us.

'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given five things which no prophet before me was given: the earth has been made for me a purifier and a place of prayer, and no prophet was to pray until he reached his prayer niche; I have been given terror [striking the enemy] from a distance of a month's journey, so that there is a month's distance between me and the polytheists, and Allah casts terror into their hearts; the Prophet used to be sent only to his particular people, but I have been sent to the jinn and mankind; the prophets used to set aside the fifth, and fire would come and consume it, but I have been commanded to distribute it among the poor of my community; and every prophet has been given his request, while I have deferred my intercession for my community." [239]

﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives﴾

It was revealed concerning al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who was a captive on that day. al-'Abbas was one of the ten who guaranteed the food of the people of Badr, and he was caught on the day of Badr. He had set out with twenty ounces of gold to feed the people with it, but the fighting broke out before that, and the twenty ounces remained with al-'Abbas and were taken from him in the battle. He asked the Prophet ﷺ to count the twenty ounces as part of his ransom, but he refused and said: "As for the wealth you set out with to use against us, I will not leave it to you." He was also required to pay the ransom for his nephews 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib and Nawfal ibn al-Harith. al-'Abbas said: "O Muhammad, you have left me to beg from Quraysh for as long as I live." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Where is the gold you gave to Umm al-Fadl at the start of your departure from Mecca, when you said to her: 'I do not know what will befall me on this journey; if some misfortune happens to me, then this is for you, for 'Abd Allah, for 'Ubayd Allah, al-Fadl and Qutham,' meaning his sons." Al-'Abbas said to him: "And how do you know that?" He said: "My Lord informed me." Al-'Abbas said: "I testify that you are truthful, and that there is no god but Allah, and that you are His servant and Messenger, and no one knew of it except Allah." That is His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives﴾, those from whom you took ransom. [240] [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi: 162.]]

Abu Muhammad and Abu Ja'far recited "min al-Asara" (with the form al-Asara); both are dialectal variants.

﴿If Allah knows any good in your hearts﴾, meaning faith, ﴿He will give you better than what has been taken from you﴾ of ransom, ﴿and forgive you﴾ your sins. Al-'Abbas said: "Allah replaced it for me with twenty slaves, all of whom trade with great wealth; the least of them trades with twenty thousand dirhams in place of the twenty ounces, and He gave me Zamzam, and I would not wish to have in exchange all the wealth of the people of Mecca, and I am awaiting forgiveness from my Lord."

Qatadah said: We were told that when the wealth of Bahrain, eighty thousand, came to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, he had performed ablution for the noon prayer. On that day he gave to no one who stood by him and refused no one who asked until he had distributed it. He commanded al-'Abbas to take from it, and he took. al-'Abbas used to say: "This is better than what was taken from us, and I hope for forgiveness."

﴿But if they intend treachery against you﴾, meaning the captives, ﴿they have already betrayed Allah before, so He gave you power over them﴾. ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated﴾ from their people, clan and homes, meaning the Muhammadan emigrants, ﴿and strove with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah, and those who sheltered [the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the emigrants] and helped﴾ against their enemies, namely the Ansar: ﴿they are allies of one another﴾, to the exclusion of their kin among the disbelievers. Ibn 'Abbas said: This refers to inheritance. They used to inherit through emigration, and Allah made the inheritance for the emigrants and the Ansar, to the exclusion of relatives by blood. Whoever believed but did not emigrate did not inherit, because he had not emigrated, nor had he given help. They acted on this until Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿And those related by blood are closer to one another in the Book of Allah﴾. So this was abrogated, and the inheritance became for blood relatives who are believers, and the people of two different religions do not inherit from one another.

﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of guardianship toward them at all until they emigrate﴾, meaning inheritance. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read the waw with a kasra, while the rest read it with a fatha; both are one in meaning. al-Kisa'i said: "al-wilayah" with a fatha means the guardianship (in inheritance and support), and "al-wilayah" with a kasra means leadership (imarah).

﴿And if they seek your help in the religion, then it is incumbent upon you to help them﴾, because they are Muslims, ﴿except against a people between you and whom there is a covenant﴾, a pact. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another﴾, in support and assistance.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning the inheritance of the polytheists who were bound by covenant. al-Suddi said: They said, "We will bequeath to our blood relatives among the polytheists," so this verse was revealed. Ibn Zayd said: The emigrant and the believer who did not emigrate did not inherit from one another, even if they were two believing brothers, because this religion in this land was weak, until the day of the Conquest, when emigration ended, and they inherited through blood ties wherever they were.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no emigration after the Conquest; rather, there is only martyrdom." [241]

Qatadah said: A man would settle between the Muslims and the polytheists and say: "If these prevail, I will be with them, and if those prevail, I will be with them." Allah refused this of them, and He revealed concerning it: ﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another﴾ [[Surah al-Anfal: 73.]], so no fire of a Muslim and [no fire] of a polytheist would be seen except for one who pays the jizyah, acknowledging the tax [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 10/72.]].

﴿Unless you do it﴾. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: unless you leave them to inherit from one another as they used to inherit. Ibn 'Abbas said: unless you take it in inheritance as I have commanded you. Ibn Jurayj said: unless you cooperate and support one another. Ibn Ishaq said: Allah the Exalted made the emigrants and the Ansar the people of His guardianship in religion to the exclusion of others, and made the disbelievers allies of one another. Then He said: ﴿Unless you do it﴾, meaning that a believer should take a disbeliever as an ally rather than a believer.
